findings.source_passage: I saw the opening maw of hell, With endless pains and sorrows there… Awful, yet bright, as lightning shone The face of my Deliverer God.
findings.why_it_matters: The hymn is a self-contained, culturally recognizable lyric; the draft reduces it to ellipses, erasing two complete stanzas including the 'opening maw of hell' and the 'lightning shone / The face of my Deliverer God' lines that critics and readers consistently quote.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore all five stanzas of the hymn verbatim; at 800-word target with compression at 1.0×, the full hymn is budgetable and its erasure is unjustified.

findings.source_passage: And what was that, shipmates? To preach the Truth to the face of Falsehood! That was it!
findings.source_locator: Near end of the 'pilot of the living God' paragraph, after 'vomited out Jonah upon the dry land'
findings.why_it_matters: This is the rhetorical climax of Mapple's second-lesson section and one of the most critically cited declarations in the chapter; its absence removes the interpretive keystone of the sermon's second movement.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the passage ending '—Jonah did the Almighty's bidding. And what was that, shipmates? To preach the Truth to the face of Falsehood! That was it!' before moving to the 'Woe' litany.

findings.source_passage: Yet this is nothing: I leave eternity to Thee; for what is man that he should live out the lifetime of his God?
findings.why_it_matters: This is the sermon's last spoken sentence before the benediction — one of the most quoted and theologically weighted lines in Moby-Dick; the draft ends the peroration two sentences early, cutting the climax entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim: 'Yet this is nothing: I leave eternity to Thee; for what is man that he should live out the lifetime of his God?' as the closing line of the 'Delight' passage.

findings.source_passage: 'Jack, he's robbed a widow;' or, 'Joe, do you mark him; he's a bigamist;' or, 'Harry lad, I guess he's the adulterer that broke jail in old Gomorrah'
findings.why_it_matters: These sailors' whispered accusations are prosodically and rhetorically distinctive — the vernacular comic irony is signature Melville and is a passage critics return to for the sermon's tonal range; its complete absence flattens the fugitive scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least one or two of the sailors' whispered accusations to preserve the tonal signature of the scene.

findings.source_passage: Woe to him who courts not dishonor! Woe to him who would not be true, even though to be false were salvation! Yea, woe to him who, as the great Pilot Paul has it, while preaching to others is himself a castaway!
findings.why_it_matters: The 'great Pilot Paul' identification and the 'to be false were salvation' clause are the most theologically charged lines of the litany and are frequently cited; their absence truncates the rhetorical structure and removes key interpretive weight.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the closing woe-clauses including 'Woe to him who courts not dishonor,' 'to be false were salvation,' and the 'great Pilot Paul' reference before the 'castaway' line.

findings.source_passage: Like one who after a night of drunken revelry hies to his bed, still reeling, but with conscience yet pricking him… for conscience is the wound, and there's naught to staunch it
findings.why_it_matters: This extended simile is one of the most distinctive rhetorical set-pieces in the chapter, blending physical sensation and moral torment in sustained periodic syntax; its omission erases a signature passage of Melvillean voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'night of drunken revelry' simile, even in compressed form, preserving 'conscience is the wound, and there's naught to staunch it.'

findings.source_passage: his ears, like two sea-shells, still multitudinously murmuring of the ocean—Jonah did the Almighty's bidding.
findings.source_locator: Second-lesson paragraph, after 'vomited out Jonah upon the dry land'
findings.why_it_matters: The simile of Jonah's ears as sea-shells 'multitudinously murmuring of the ocean' is a prosodically unique and critically remarked image; its absence removes a distinctive sensory signature of the sermon's climax.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'his ears, like two sea-shells, still multitudinously murmuring of the ocean' before the 'what was that, shipmates' rhetorical question.

summary: The draft commits three high-severity signature losses (the closing line of the 'Delight' peroration, the 'Truth to the face of Falsehood' climax, and the full hymn text) plus four medium-severity losses, requiring regeneration.
